subject: Questionnaire: International Data Processing & DPF controls — NorthernBridge Health
messages:
From: Emma Shearer <emma.shearer@northbridgehealth.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@northbridgehealth.com
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: RFI — International processing, DPF controls, and DPA annex mapping

Sean —

Thanks for taking this. NorthernBridge Health is running a procurement for inference providers and we need granular technical answers on international transfers and the Data Processing Framework (DPF) measures you apply. I’ve attached our RFI template (NBH_RFI_Template.xlsx). Please provide answers to the following high-priority items by EOD next Wednesday (2026-02-18):

1) Where does tokenized request data and KV/cache state execute for EU-origin requests? Are there model variants or routing policies that keep inference entirely within eu-west-1?
2) For dedicated/private deployments we may request on-prem inference. Please confirm what operational runbook and responsibilities Redwood provides versus NBH (network, KMS handling, patching windows).
3) Data deletion SLA: we need a confirmed maximum timeframe for purging customer data from hot caches, persistent logs, and backups. Do you support a sub-30-day purge for ephemeral states?
4) Subprocessor list and whether any third-party model-serving libraries perform remote calls that could cause unexpected cross-border egress.
5) Do you provide a DPA annex mapping to the EU-US transfer mechanism (DPF/SCC alternatives) and a controls matrix we can include in our vendor assessment?

Please include any evidence artifacts you can share (control mappings, KMS key handling notes, SOC2 page). If you prefer a technical call, suggest times and we’ll coordinate.

Best,
Emma
Procurement Lead — NorthernBridge Health
attachments: NBH_RFI_Template.xlsx

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: RFI — International processing, DPF controls, and DPA annex mapping

Team —

Forwarding NorthernBridge’s RFI. High priority: they’ve asked for answers by EOD 2/18. Can we pull a concise technical package and an initial mapping for the DPA annex? Owners: Marissa — lead on control mapping and evidence. Karthik — lead on deployment/runbook and on-prem responsibilities. Ben — please confirm subprocessor list and any third-party network calls.

Key asks I want covered in the response:
- In-region inference guarantees for EU traffic (routing policy, model pinning)
- KV cache residency and whether ephemeral state is persisted anywhere outside the requested region
- Clear deletion SLAs for ephemeral and persistent logs/backups
- On-prem runbook summary (what we do/what customer does) and KMS boundary points
- A short control matrix PDF (redwood-dpf-mapping-v1.pdf)

Timelines: draft answers by Monday EOD (2/16) so I can review and send final by 2/18.

Thanks —
Sean
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Feb 2026 08:27:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: RFI — International processing, DPF controls, and DPA annex mapping

Sean / team —

I’ve pulled a draft control matrix and initial answers. See highlights below and attached redwood-dpf-mapping-v1.pdf (summary + evidence references). Full attachment has links to our SOC 2 summary page (redacted) and the KMS responsibility matrix. Highlights:

1) Routing / in-region execution: Hosted API routes by default based on customer region. For EU-origin tokens, requests are routed to our eu-west-1 cluster and served by model instances pinned to that region. We offer a model-variant pin to force both inference and KV/cache to remain in eu-west-1. Exceptions: if the customer chooses global routing for latency/cost, traffic can be routed elsewhere (documented).

2) KV cache and ephemeral state: The runtime keeps KV cache in-memory on the serving instance; for hosted eu-west-1 that memory and any ephemeral cache stay on eu-west-1 hosts. We do not persist KV cache to multi-region object storage by default. If a customer requests cross-region backups for redundancy, that is an opt-in config and documented in the runbook.

3) Deletion SLA: Hot ephemeral cache eviction is immediate on instance tear-down; however, operational logs and diagnostic traces are retained by default for 90 days. For procurement-grade contracts we can offer an SLA with a 30-day maximum for customer-identifying logs and a 7-day target for ephemeral caches, subject to audit and forensics carve-outs. I’ve marked the deletion SLA item for legal to confirm final wording.

4) Subprocessors: I pulled the current list — primary cloud providers (AWS eu-west-1), CDN provider, monitoring/observability vendor, and a kernel-optimization vendor used only in our runtime build pipeline. None of our runtime libraries initiate remote calls to external inference endpoints during live requests. I’ll ask Ben to paste the current subprocessor list into the doc.

5) DPA annex mapping: Draft included. It maps our controls to the standard DPF elements and provides a suggested annex text for inclusion in the customer DPA.

Attachments: redwood-dpf-mapping-v1.pdf (matrix + evidence pointers). I will follow up with granular log retention excerpts and the SOC2 evidence pointer.

Marissa
Principal Privacy Engineer — Redwood Inference
attachments: redwood-dpf-mapping-v1.pdf

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Feb 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: RFI — International processing, DPF controls, and DPA annex mapping

Quick note from procurement/subprocessors side —

Current subprocessors we should include in the NBH response:
- AWS (eu-west-1) — compute, EBS, S3 for optional backups
- Cloudfront (EU POPs) — optional for model artifacts distribution
- Datadog — monitoring/alerting (no PII ingestion; metrics only)
- FastPaths Labs — kernel optimization libraries (build-time only, no runtime network calls)
- VaultCorp (KMS integration partner) — used for HSM-managed key exchange on private deployments

No runtime third-party inference calls. We audit our build pipeline to ensure no network callbacks from model-serving binaries. I’ve attached a short KMS handling note for private deployments.

Ben
Vendor Risk & Procurement — Redwood Inference
attachments: kms-key-handling.txt

From: Emma Shearer <emma.shearer@northbridgehealth.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@northbridgehealth.com
Date: Tue, 17 Feb 2026 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: RFI — International processing, DPF controls, and DPA annex mapping

Thanks Sean/Marissa/Ben — this is helpful. A few clarifying points before we close the questionnaire: 

- Deletion SLA: NBH requires a maximum of 30 days for purging customer-identifying logs and any persisted inference artifacts; ephemeral cache is acceptable at a 7-day target but we’d prefer 24–48 hours if possible. Can you confirm firm commitments you can include in a DPA annex?
- Private on-prem runbook: can you send the summary of responsibilities (network peering, KMS key custody steps, patching cadence) as a one-page checklist? That will speed our internal legal review.
- We’d like a short statement confirming that no model-serving runtime performs outbound requests to third-party services during live inference beyond calls to your internal telemetry endpoint. If that statement is OK, we can mark that as closed.

Can we do a 30-minute technical call on Thu 2/18 10:00–10:30 PT? Let me know and I’ll send a calendar invite.

Regards,
Emma
Procurement Lead — NorthernBridge Health

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emma Shearer <emma.shearer@northbridgehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 16:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: RFI — International processing, DPF controls, and DPA annex mapping

Emma —

Thanks — meeting confirmed for Thu 2/18 10:00 PT (please send the invite). Quick answers ahead of the call:
- Deletion SLA: we can offer a contractual option of 30 days for customer-identifying logs and artifacts (enterprise SLA) and we target 24–48 hours for ephemeral cache eviction where customers select aggressive retention settings. Final legal text will be in the DPA annex.
- On-prem runbook: Karthik will drop a one-page checklist into the Drive link and we’ll attach to the RFI response (private-deploy-runbook.pdf).
- Runtime outbound calls: Confirmed — production model-serving runtime does not make outbound calls to third-party services during live requests beyond telemetry to our internal collection endpoint (which can be disabled for Private deployments).

Marissa and Karthik — please upload the one-page runbook and updated mapping to the Drive link by EOD today. I’ll send the compiled response to NBH after review.

Sean
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
